observations.explanation: The paper describes a two-phase localization-and-repair pipeline, with hierarchical localization and patch generation, filtering, and voting; it contrasts this with agent-based tool-use planning (PDF pp. 2–5).

The paper reports 82/300 resolved (27.33%) and $0.34 average cost (PDF pp. 6–7). Its ablation reports 70 fixes with one sample, 78 with multiple samples and majority voting, and 82 after test filtering (PDF p. 8).
The authors report a manual classification of SWE-bench Lite issues and define Lite-S as a 252-problem subset; Table 4 reports 71 resolved (28.17%) by AGENTLESS (PDF pp. 9–10).
The paper explicitly says it could not run commercial tools on the modified problems and instead excluded problematic cases from their prior results for the Lite-S evaluation (PDF p. 10).
